Part of the argument behind a subscription based game (universally online games, never anything else) is that it enables the developers to maintain and expand the servers as needed, and keep sufficient maintenance/support crew on the payroll. It's not a game that is just shipped out and ignored, people have to be paid wages to make sure everything is running how it should be.

Beyond that, a steady income enables developers to shunt more resources into a steady stream of content development. New areas, new quests, etc. In a vacuum, surely you could agree that a company would be incentivized to keep a game enjoyable if the brunt of their income comes from players. In contrast, a development company would not be so keen to churn out new content on a pay-once model, as they already made their money from initial sales, and continued development doesn't really make economic sense.
